component.name: MINIKeyboard
component.summary: Set up small USB macro keyboards

description.p: Writes key settings to small USB macro keyboards — the ones sold with anything from a single knob to 21 keys, and up to four knobs.

For each key and knob action (rotate left, press, rotate right) it sets key presses, a media key or a mouse action on layers 1–3, and the keyboard’s lighting. A keyboard that doesn’t say its shape gets the layout you pick, and the app remembers it.

Linux lets an app open a USB device only when a udev rule gives it to the signed-in user, so after installing, add the rule once: the app shows it, with the commands to copy, under How to Allow…, and the project’s help page explains it.
